title: Vector geometry helpers
instructions:
Implement `Vector2` in `vector2.py`, a small immutable-by-convention point/vector class.
Coordinates and scalar arguments are finite real numbers; nonnumeric inputs are outside scope.
The public attributes `x` and `y` are floats. No operator overloads or equality method are required.
Implement exactly these public operations:
- `Vector2(x=0.0, y=0.0)` stores floating-point coordinates.
- `add(other: Vector2) -> Vector2` returns the componentwise sum.
- `scale(factor: float) -> Vector2` multiplies both coordinates by the factor.
- `dot(other: Vector2) -> float` returns the dot product.
- `distance_to(other: Vector2) -> float` returns Euclidean point distance.
- `normalized() -> Vector2` returns a vector of length one in the same direction.
  The zero vector raises `ValueError`.
All operations leave their inputs unchanged. Every vector result must be a new object, including
scaling by one and normalizing a unit vector. Floating-point comparisons allow normal rounding error.

## Files
- `vector2.py`
